name: Inter (Internazionale) 1963-65, Grande Inter under Helenio Herrera
scopeNote: Seasons 1963/64 and 1964/65: Serie A 1964/65 title, European Cups 1964 (3-1 v Real Madrid, Vienna, 27 May 1964) and 1965 (1-0 v Benfica, San Siro, 27 May 1965), Intercontinental Cup 1964 (v Independiente, played Sept 1964 inside 1964/65 season counting). The 1962/63 Scudetto is outside the period. The 1965 Intercontinental Cup (Sept 1965) is EXCLUDED as it belongs to 1965/66. Partial date: first competitive match of 1963/64 not verified on a page (start 1963-09, from memory). End 1965-06-06 is the last Serie A matchday (2-2 v Torino, inter.it); the Intercontinental Cup 1964 was played in Sept 1964 (three matches, inter.it). Manager spell dates 1960-06/1968-06 are approximate (from memory, not verified). stated-view of Herrera is undated/retrospective, hence a gap. Style label: catenaccio is the popular and press term; sources describe a man-to-man marking back line with a libero (Picchi) plus an attacking left-back (Facchetti), and counter-attacking transitions; Mazzola says only about 6 of 46 matches were played in a catenaccio way (mostly away European ties), so the label is too simple. Almost all evidence is retrospective (2010-2025); no contemporaneous 1963-65 sources were reached.
openQuestions: Peiro arrival date (summer 1964) not stated on the inter.it page; squad-building evidence is weak (only the arrival and a stable XI), nothing verified on youth debuts or veterans minutes.
Exact dates of first and last competitive matches in the period not verified; from memory Serie A 1963/64 opened in September 1963 and 1964/65 ended in June 1965.
From search summary only (UEFA, unverified): Inter lost a 1963/64 Serie A playoff to Bologna; one source lists Serie A titles 1963/64, others 1962/63, 1964/65, 1965/66. Needs a page check.
The Intercontinental Cup 1964 tie, a third decisive match is recalled from memory; Picchi article gives only 1-0 away and 2-0 in Milan.

SI and Sportsenators/Picchi pieces disagree on shape: 5-3-2 with four man-markers and a sweeper (SI), back four plus sweeper (TFT), 4-3-3 line-up (Sportsenators). Counting differs by whether sweeper and Facchetti are counted as defenders.

Mazzola quote that only about 6 matches were catenaccio is a player claim; Sacchi (via Wilson) says Herrera adopted libero/counter style after a bad result early 1960s; FourFourTwo says Herrera won nothing with the early free-scoring side.
Zonal vs man marking: sources found say man-marking; Sportskeeda/FM sites mention a zonal fusion, not read (tier D).
Not covered by verified evidence: pressing intensity, possession figures, set-piece routines (only isolated goals), youth/debut minutes.

sources.evidence: Herrera’s side had lost 3-1 away to Liverpool and, before the return leg, according to Wilson, Bill Shankly had claimed an Italian journalist had told him: “You will never be allowed to win.” Inter won 3-0 in a game riddled with controversy.

sources.title: The incomparable legacy of Helenio Herrera (These Football Times)
sources.evidence: He embraced his players before kick-off, and held one-on-one meetings known as ‘confessions’.

sources.title: The incomparable legacy of Helenio Herrera (These Football Times)
sources.evidence: Cultivated what became known as the ritiro. They were no-nonsense training camps where players were locked up in hotels for days, surrounded by staff, pitches and equipment. The intention was to increase concentration before games.

sources.title: The incomparable legacy of Helenio Herrera (These Football Times)
sources.evidence: Armando Picchi, a commanding sweeper, once challenge Herrera’s authority and was shipped out to AS Varese. The only idler to survive was Mario Corso, an ingenious left-footed winger, whom Herrera constantly tried to offload, but who enjoyed the admiration and decisive support of Moratti. A player who pleased Herrera more was Suárez. In 1960, the Ballon d’Or winner followed him from Barça to Inter.

statedView.quote: A small number of short, very quick passes to get to the opposition’s goal in as little time as possible. There is almost no place for dribbling. It’s a tool, not a system.
To the Catalans, I talked: ‘Colours of Catalonia, play for your nation.’ And to the foreigners, I talked money... You have twenty-five players, you don’t say the same thing to everyone.
The word ‘wizard’ doesn’t belong to football. ‘Passion’ and ‘strength’ are football words.
I doubt whether they would beat us in the final in Lisbon. After all, we only need one goal.
When I hear about Inter playing catenaccio, I have to say we played about six matches with catenaccio and 40 matches with attacking football (Mazzola, not Herrera)
